steps.title: should and have to
steps.html:
MeaningExample
shouldit's a good ideaYou should book online.
shouldn'tit's a bad ideaYou shouldn't take a taxi from the airport.
have to / has toit's a ruleYou have to show your ticket.
don't have tothere is no rule — it's your choiceYou don't have to pay for children.
questionDo I have to book? · Should I take a coat?

After should and have to the verb is the base form — no to after should.

don't have to does NOT mean it is forbidden. It means you can choose.

To say something is forbidden, use can't: You can't take photos here.

Learners often write You should to book. There is no to after should.

steps.title: You are going to read a rule book for visitors to Japan.
steps.sub: What do you think is rude there?

steps.title: Six rules for a first visit to Japan
steps.html:
1. You have to take your shoes off in a house, and often in a restaurant too. You should look at the floor: if there are slippers, take your shoes off.

2. You don't have to leave a tip. In fact you shouldn't — some people think it is rude.

3. You should be quiet on the train. You can talk, but people don't use phones there, and nobody eats.

4. You have to buy a ticket before you get on the bus in some cities, and after in others. You should ask.

5. You shouldn't eat while you walk. It isn't a rule, but it looks strange.

6. You don't have to speak Japanese, but you should learn two words: sumimasen (excuse me) and arigatou (thank you). They open every door.
